title: Apple Is Generating Sell Signals - Do Not Ignore Them
text:
Apple Is Generating Sell Signals - Do Not Ignore Them By aapl 
Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) was reviewed just last month and I wrote that, "With a couple shorter-term bearish divergences on APPL, traders who have a high average cost should pay closer attention to the price action especially later this week." With AAPL down more than 3% today a fresh look at the charts and indicators seems like a good idea. 
In this daily bar chart of AAPL, below, we can see not only that AAPL closed under the 50-day moving average line last month but the slope of the line has turned down. The still rising 200-day line intersects a little below $160 and that is not that far away now. The pace of volume has been heavier since the middle of January telling us that sellers are more anxious. 
The On-Balance-Volume (OBV) line peaked in early November and shows a bearish divergence to the price action which made a new high in January. The Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) oscillator gave us two signals recently. In the middle of January it turned down for a take profits sell signal and more recently crossed below the zero line for an outright sell signal. 
In this weekly bar chart of AAPL below, going back three years, we can see (below) mixed signals. Prices are still above the rising 40-week moving average line but a test of the line could happen as early as next week. The weekly OBV line looks like it has "stalled out". The MACD oscillator on this longer time frame has just crossed to the downside for another take profits sell signal. 
Bottom line: Apple products are highly loved by millions. Apple the stock is highly loved, I believe, by millions of investors. What sometimes happens when a stock is loved is that investors will be slow to recognize a turn or reversal of fortunes. This is not a moral failing -- it is just human nature. The problem becomes an issue when sell signals are generated and people become stubborn and ignore the sign or argue with it. I am right and the market is wrong. 
Strategy: AAPL is below the declining 50-day line and could break the 200-day average -- this is a classic sell signal in my book. Get an email alert each time I write an article for Real Money. Click the "+Follow" next to my byline to this article. More From Bruce Kamich
